subject.title: Agent confabulates completed actions on Telegram surface — same config works reliably on Claude Code/Codex

question: Should this Telegram/ACP false-completion class be fixed in core with a source-turn verification/fail-closed invariant, or should core document the current delivery behavior and route broad action-claim verification to a ClawHub/plugin package?
rationale: Current main has prompt guidance, warning-only delivery diagnostics, plugin hook surfaces, and adjacent open issues, but no product decision tying arbitrary visible success claims to tool-ledger evidence in Telegram/ACP turns.

options.title: Define A Narrow Core Invariant
options.body: Specify which Telegram/ACP source-turn claims require tool evidence and what user-visible diagnostic, retry, or suppression behavior should occur when evidence is missing.

options.title: Route Broad Verification To ClawHub
options.body: Treat natural-language success-claim verification as plugin policy, keep core docs and hooks sufficient, and close this issue once maintainers explicitly accept that boundary.

options.title: Wait For Adjacent Recovery First
options.body: Resolve the narrower stranded-final recovery PR before revisiting broader claimed-action verification, preserving this issue as the broader policy tracker.

recommendation.title: Define A Narrow Core Invariant
recommendation.body: Specify which Telegram/ACP source-turn claims require tool evidence and what user-visible diagnostic, retry, or suppression behavior should occur when evidence is missing.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest available history signal on both the current diagnostics-only behavior and the maintainer decision that broad claim verification can be plugin/ClawHub-scoped.
